overview.title: Crocodiles and gardens near the coast
overview.p1: Crocoparc is a purpose-built park with Nile crocodiles, walkways and planted gardens. It is one of the most popular organised outings from Agadir for families and anyone wanting a break from pure beach days.
overview.p2: Paths are mostly easy. Combine it with a coastal stop or return to the city for the afternoon. Check opening hours and ticket prices before you go.

gallery.title: Park scenes
gallery.subtitle: Crocodiles and gardens south of the city.

food.title: Eat at or near Crocoparc
food.p1: The park usually has a café or snack options on site — enough for a short visit. A fuller meal can wait for Agadir on the way back.
food.li1: On-site café for drinks and snacks.
food.li5: Cards may be accepted at the ticket desk.

1.title: Getting there
1.desc: Taxi or organised transfer from Agadir. Confirm return transport before entering.

2.title: Tickets
2.desc: Buy at the entrance; check current prices and any online options.

3.title: Heat
3.desc: Morning visits are more comfortable in summer; bring sun protection.

q1.question: How far is Crocoparc from Agadir?
q1.answer: About 30–40 minutes south of the city by road.

q2.question: Is it good for children?
q2.answer: Yes — it is one of the main family attractions near Agadir.

q3.question: How long do I need?
q3.answer: Two to three hours is typical for the park paths and enclosures.

q4.question: Can I combine with the beach?
q4.answer: Yes — morning at Crocoparc, afternoon back on Agadir Beach is a common plan.

q5.question: Are the crocodiles real Nile crocodiles?
q5.answer: The park is known for its Nile crocodile collection; follow all barrier and safety rules.
